column1: # A COMPRESSED FLOAT'S RANGE IS HELD AT FLOAT32 (docs/SPEC-TABLES.md §3.3):
# the value is narrowed to float32 and held to the float32 nearest each
# declared end. Probe.schema is the unit: under max = 0.1 the end is 0.1f
# (bits 3dcccccd) and under min = -0.3 it is -0.3f (bits be99999a); one float32
# step past either (3dccccce, be99999b) is off the range.
# Every port that saves a compressed float runs every row:
#   read   read <input>.<form>.bin (form variable or fixed) or <input>.json
#          (form json) into <root>. `refused` owes a refusal; a stem owes
#          acceptance, and then saving the value in <root>'s own form (V the
#          variable form, F the fixed form) owes <stem>.variable.bin or
#          <stem>.fixed.bin byte for byte: save at the end, read, save again.
#   write  read <input>.json into <root>, set <path> to the float32 whose bits
#          are <bits> IN THE NATIVE VALUE, after the load, and save <form>.
#          `refused` owes the writer's refusal; a stem owes <stem>.<form>.bin.
# ends.json holds both ends ("0.1", "-0.3"); past-max.json and past-min.json
# spell the float32 one step past each ("0.10000001", "-0.30000004").
# narrow.json spells decimals that are NOT float32 values but narrow onto the
# be99999a, below the double -0.3): a port that tests the double before it
# narrows refuses them, and they owe the ends bytes. over-max.json and
# over-min.json spell 3.5e38 and -3.5e38, past float32's own max: §16.2 refuses
# a value the field's width cannot hold (kind_mismatch, before any range test),
# so it never lands, clamped or not. nan-token.json and inf-token.json carry
# tokens JSON has no spelling for (malformed). nan, pinf and ninf .bin are the
# binary forms' non-finite values (refused non_finite_float, §3.3), and the
# write rows with bits 7fc00000, 7f800000 and ff800000 owe the writer's
# refusal. Every .bin other than ends is ends.<form>.bin with one float's bits
# replaced, so no writer is asked to make them. internal/tablewire's
